gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-sarala: Red Hat Display draws every stroke like a marker, with visible daylight inside each curve. And Sarala follows with distinct gaps in its letters and a thickness like neon glass tubing, so the two glow rather than clash.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-sawarabi-gothi: Contemporary and bold, Red Hat Display holds a uniform line with no calligraphic modulation at all, every curve left open. Sawarabi Gothic stays low-key beneath it.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-shanti: Marker-bold and modern up top. Red Hat Display has bowls that never thin at the sides, and Shanti follows with a gentle entry into the e's eye, so the two feel like relatives with different volumes.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-shippori-antiq: A constant-width line, like a marker, gives Red Hat Display its look, with daylight showing inside every curve. Shippori Antique reads smoothly onward.
Shippori Antique B1 has the plain line of a stencil brush. Red Hat Display above it shares that fixed-width stroke, so heading and text feel cut from the same marker, only louder up top.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-sn-pro: Bold, marker-like and unbroken. Red Hat Display keeps its line width uninterrupted on every letter, while SN Pro carries open curves throughout the alphabet, so a long passage flows without snagging.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-sour-gummy: Contemporary and confident, Red Hat Display has a line that glides under the eye like wire. Sour Gummy brings wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp, which is the pair's real strength.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-source-sans-3: Bold and contemporary, Red Hat Display uses strokes with no thin or thick swings, just a steady marker line. But Source Sans 3 has an a whose lower bowl opens to breathe, and that gives the pair its clarity.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-spinnaker: Spinnaker reads cleanly, its apertures keeping counters linked to outside space. Red Hat Display does round letters whose rims match the stems best, while Spinnaker handles the quieter work of text.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-stick: Stick reads as tubelike, constant-weight lines with exits wide enough to pass light through. Red Hat Display shares that marker-like steadiness, so the pair's strongest quality is a single line weight carried from heading to text.
